record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Quantum Information Theory
record.context_brief: Lockability of operational entanglement and key measures
record.original_question: Are two-way distillable entanglement and the secret key rate lockable, meaning extremely sensitive to the loss of a single qubit by one of the partners?

evidence.quote: Are two-way distillible entanglement and secret key rate lockable?
An entanglement measure is lockable, if it is extremely sensitive to the loss of a single qubit by one of the partners [HHHO04].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setting. Let $\mathcal{H}_A$ and $\mathcal{H}_B$ be finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces and let $\rho_{AB}$ be a bipartite quantum state on $\mathcal{H}_A\otimes\mathcal{H}_B$. Denote by $D(\rho_{AB})$ the two-way distillable entanglement of $\rho_{AB}$ (the optimal asymptotic rate at which maximally entangled qubit pairs can be extracted from many copies of $\rho_{AB}$ using local operations and two-way classical communication), and by $K(\rho_{AB})$ the (two-way) distillable secret key rate (the optimal asymptotic rate at which a shared secret key, secure against an eavesdropper purifying $\rho_{AB}$, can be extracted by local operations and public classical communication).

Definition (lockability). A function $E$ on bipartite states is called lockable if there exist sequences of states $\rho^{(n)}_{AA'BB'}$ on $\mathcal{H}_A\otimes\mathcal{H}_{A'}\otimes\mathcal{H}_B\otimes\mathcal{H}_{B'}$, with $\dim\mathcal{H}_{A'}=2$ (a single qubit held by Alice) and arbitrary $\dim\mathcal{H}_{B'}$, such that
$$\limsup_{n\to\infty}\bigl(E(\rho^{(n)}_{AA'BB'}) - E(\mathrm{tr}_{A'}\rho^{(n)}_{AA'BB'})\bigr)=+\infty,$$
i.e. tracing out one qubit on Alice's side can decrease $E$ by an arbitrarily large amount.

Question. Are the two-way distillable entanglement $D$ and the distillable secret key rate $K$ lockable in the above sense?
artifact.status_search_result: The Open Quantum Problems platform maintained by IQOQI Vienna lists the lockability of two-way distillable entanglement and of the secret key rate as an unresolved problem. While several other entanglement measures (entanglement of formation, entanglement cost, logarithmic negativity, squashed entanglement) have been shown to be lockable, the lockability of $D$ and $K$ remains open.
